About Us
Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.
The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.
Role Summary
The Infotainment Platform team at Rivian Volkswagen Technologies is looking for a skilled Software Engineer to join our Automotive Software team. We are developing the next generation, Android-based in-vehicle experience that will be deployed across all future electric vehicles in the Rivian and Volkswagen Group portfolios. You will work on the architecture, integration, and optimization of both display and input subsystems for our next-generation infotainment platforms. In this role, you will own the end-to-end pipeline from the low-level hardware drivers (touch controllers, display panels, physical buttons) up through the OS frameworks (Linux, QNX, Android Automotive) to ensure a seamless, highly responsive, and visually flawless user experience.
Join us in driving the future of automotive infotainment!
Responsibilities
Display & Graphics Pipeline: Develop, integrate, and maintain display drivers and compositor frameworks (e.g., DRM/KMS, SurfaceFlinger, Wayland, OpenWFD) for complex, multi-display automotive topologies.
Touch & Input Subsystems: Develop and integrate drivers and middleware for touch panels (capacitive, resistive) and physical infotainment buttons (e.g., hard keys, rotary dials, steering wheel controls). Optimize input processing, gesture recognition, multi-touch coordination, and noise filtering within the OS input frameworks (e.g., Android InputFlinger, Linux evdev).
Performance Optimization: Tune the complete glass-to-glass pipeline. Optimize frame rates, visual quality (color accuracy, white point tuning), and touch/button latency to ensure a fluid, highly responsive user experience.
Hardware Bring-Up & Integration: Partner closely with hardware vendors and SoC partners to bring up new display panels (LCD, OLED) and input interfaces via standard buses (MIPI DSI, I2C, SPI) and SerDes links.
System-Level Debugging: Investigate and resolve complex display and input issues (e.g., screen freezes, visual artifacts, touch ghosting, missed button presses, dropped frames) using software profilers, gdb, JTAG, and logic analyzers.
Feature Development: Implement advanced system features such as dynamic backlight control, power sequencing, resolution switching, fault monitoring, and multi-display synchronization.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Hardware engineers, UI/UX designers, and System teams to define requirements, document software architectures, and ensure compliance with automotive safety and EMC requirements.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
3+ years of proven experience in embedded software development or platform engineering, specifically focusing on display panels, touch screens, and hardware input technologies.
Strong proficiency in C/C++ programming.
Deep understanding of embedded operating systems such as Linux, QNX, or Android Automotive OS.
Solid grasp of display and input frameworks (e.g., Linux DRM/KMS, Android SurfaceFlinger/InputManager).
Experience with hardware peripherals and interfaces (I2C, SPI, UART, MIPI DSI).
Excellent problem-solving, system-level debugging, and teamwork skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience bringing up automotive infotainment platforms on major SoCs (e.g., Qualcomm Snapdragon, NXP).
Familiarity with graphics libraries and hardware compositors (OpenGL ES, Vulkan, HWC).
Experience with automotive communication protocols (CAN, Automotive Ethernet).
Familiarity with display virtualization (VirtIO-GPU) and hypervisor environments (e.g., QNX, Gunyah).
Proficiency with performance profiling tools like Systrace, Perfetto, and vendor-specific GPU profilers.
Total Rewards
We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program.
Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. This role is also eligible for equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), subject to board approval and the terms of our equity incentive plans, including applicable vesting requirements.
In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. US-based · Remote-friendly · Flexible hours
Vision Elements is a computational-sciences consultancy. We solve the core, hard problems at the heart of very different domains: computer vision and 3D, medical and scientific imaging, signal and sensor processing, applied machine learning. Clients bring us problems that call for algorithmic depth outside their team's specialism; we reduce them to their mathematical essence and build the algorithm that works.
Who we're looking for
A junior with a real passion for math and physics, who lights up at a scientific challenge. Like us, you should be fascinated by the variety of problems, industries, and domains, seeing it as the best part of the job rather than chaos. Above all, you should enjoy the reduction: taking a messy, domain-specific problem and stripping it to its clean mathematical core. One month it's geometry and cameras, the next a biosignal or a reconstruction problem. We bring the domain context and mentorship; you bring rigor, curiosity, and the itch to make something actually work.
What you'll do
• Prototype algorithms for real client problems across imaging, vision, 3D, signals, and ML, from first principles to working code.
• Run and analyze experiments: design benchmarks, quantify what works, and turn results into clear, honest conclusions.
• Reduce problems to their core: find the right mathematical formulation, then the simplest method that solves it robustly.
• Work shoulder-to-shoulder with senior scientists, learning how hard problems get scoped, de-risked, and delivered.
You likely have
• An MSc or PhD (completed or in progress) in a quantitative field: CS, EE, physics, applied math, biomedical or mechanical engineering, or similar.
• Strong mathematical foundations: linear algebra, probability and statistics, optimization, and/or signal processing.
• Fluency in Python and a scientific stack (NumPy/SciPy, PyTorch or similar).
• The habit of thinking a problem through before coding it, and the discipline to verify results.
Nice to have
• Exposure to any of: deep learning, classical computer vision, DSP, medical imaging, 3D geometry, or numerical methods.
• C/C++ or GPU/CUDA experience for performance-critical work.
• A publication, thesis, or side project you're proud to walk us through.
• Comfort switching domains, with genuine excitement about doing so.
The engagement
• Flexible & open: part-time contract or full-time; we'll shape it around the right person. A strong part-time fit can grow into more over time.
• Built for students: MSc and PhD candidates welcome. Hours flex with coursework, academic research, and life.
• US-based, remote-friendly: work from anywhere in the US. Occasional overlap with the team for reviews and pairing.
To apply
: send your résumé with a short note on a hard problem you enjoyed solving. Compensation discussed directly, competitive for the level.

About This Role
As a
Spacecraft Avionics Test Engineer II
, you'll play a key role in the design and operation of critical systems that simulate and stress-test flight hardware to prove it is ready for its trip to space. Familiarity with common sensor types, including thermocouples, RTDs and 4-20mA devices.
Proficiency with Git source control system.

Prior experience standing up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and driving and operating system-level tests.
Familiarity with Unix environments.
Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.
Experience operating environmental test equipment (vibration shakers, TVAC chambers, or thermal chambers).
Strong project or program management skills.

SFS is the Unified Forecast System’s (UFS) global-coupled seasonal forecasting application, which will replace CFSv2. The work location is at the NOAA Center for Weather and Climate Prediction (NCWCP) in Riverdale Park, MD.
The Ideal Physical Scientist and Seasonal Forecast System Developer will be able to work a hybrid schedule, working 2 days per week from the NOAA Center for Weather and Climate Prediction (NCWCP) office in College Park, MD, and the remaining 3 days per week from home.
Duties of the Seasonal Forecast System Developer will include the following
The candidate will perform job duties in a high-quality, independent, and collaborative way, developing and applying innovative methods for the primary work areas. The candidate will work with OMD scientists and external collaborators to develop and evaluate the current and future operational seasonal and marine forecasting systems. The candidate will work with the UFS infrastructure in designing and evaluating the global coupled ensemble forecasting systems for long range forecasting. Detailed responsibilities will include at least two aspects or more of the following areas.
Development of global coupled Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models.
Development of marine (ocean and sea ice) forecast systems.
Development of subseasonal to seasonal probabilistic forecasting systems.
Development of AI/ML techniques for seasonal and marine forecasting systems.
Designing and conducting retrospective ensemble experiments and re-forecasts.
Exploring initial or analysis uncertainties, and/or model uncertainties (or model stochastic perturbations).
Analysis and evaluation of S2S probabilistic forecasts, and applications of multi-model ensembles and statistical post processing.
The Seasonal Forecast System Developer selected should have the following
A Master or PhD’s Degree or equivalence in atmospheric sciences or meteorology, oceanic, mathematics, or related physical science with 1-2 years of experience in the area of global coupled ensemble forecast system development, sub-seasonal to seasonal prediction, numerical prediction, and/or AI/ML foundational prediction models. Candidates must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident Card Holder to qualify (please indicate in your cover letter).
Demonstrated knowledge, skills, and abilities in the following areas
Advanced knowledge of S2S prediction and experience in developing ensemble based and coupled SFS for research and operational implementation.
Development of AI-ML methods for NWP and/or geophysical applications.
Excellent knowledge and skills of modern programming languages and object-oriented languages, such as FORTRAN and Python.
Skills and knowledge of the High Performance Computing (HPC) environment with strong scripting capabilities.
Proficient with modern software development practices and version control software (e.g., Git and GitHub).
Demonstrated skill in communicating effectively with scientists of diverse backgrounds on technical details of the work plan and present results accurately and clearly in both oral and written form.
Ability to work independently on complex problems in a team and fast-paced environment and demonstrated skill in performing tasks requiring organization and attention to detail.
Ability to support team initiatives, demonstrate respect for team members, and seek team consensus.
The Ideal Seasonal Forecast System Developer will have the following
Deep knowledge of ensemble strategy, reanalysis/reforecasting, and IC uncertainty.
Familiarity with operational NWP and/or an operational forecasting environment and experience with advanced technical workflows.
Experience with UFS applications and UFS infrastructure and knowledge of earth system modeling.
Familiarity with agile software development practices.

Job Title: Associate, Software Engineer

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44833.description_preview:
Description
Shape what comes next | Discover careers in Tech
At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. This is where ambition meets opportunity and, where the impact of what you build helps define what comes next, for customers and for you.
What's in it for you? An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.
Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable services in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your code directly impact millions of customers worldwide?
At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. Customer obsession is part of our company DNA, which has made us one of the world's most beloved brands.
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.
Our SDE interns use modern technology to solve complex problems while seeing their work's impact first-hand. The challenges SDE interns solve at Amazon are meaningful and influence millions of customers, sellers, and products globally. We seek individuals passionate about creating new products, features, and services while managing ambiguity in an environment where development cycles are measured in weeks, not years.
At Amazon, we believe in ownership at every level. As a SDE intern, you'll own the entire lifecycle of your code - from design through deployment and ongoing operations. This ownership mindset, combined with our commitment to operational excellence, ensures we deliver the highest quality solutions for our customers.
We're looking for curious minds who think big and want to define tomorrow's technology. At Amazon, you'll grow into the high-impact engineer you know you can be, supported by a culture of learning and mentorship. Every day brings exciting new challenges and opportunities for personal growth.
________________________
By applying to this position, your application will be considered for Summer 2027 internship roles. All intern roles require in-person work and are 12 weeks in duration, starting in May/June and ending in August/September. Applicants will be considered at all locations we host interns in the United States.
Please Note That The Majority Of Our Internships Are In The Summer Of 2027 And Applicants Will Be Processed Based On Business Need; However, There May Be Additional Openings That Include The Following Periods
Winter 2027 (Start January/February; End April/May)
Fall 2027 (Start August/September; End November/December)
During the application process, you will be given the opportunity to select a preference or interest in other seasonal start dates. Please note that placement in a non-summer season is not guaranteed and is subject to availability.
Amazon internships across all seasons are full-time positions, and interns should expect to work in office, Monday-Friday, up to 40 hours per week typically between 8am-5pm. Specific team norms around working hours will be communicated by your manager. Interns should not have conflicts such as classes or other employment during the Amazon work-day. Applicants should have a minimum of one quarter/semester/trimester remaining in their studies after their internship concludes.
We will take your location preferences into consideration. Preferences are based on business availability and are not guaranteed. Applicants will be considered at all locations we host interns in the United States including but not limited to:
WA (Redmond)
***Locations are subject to change***
Export Control Requirement
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
During your application, you will have the opportunity to highlight your expertise in one or more of these specialized areas:

Database Systems
Quantum Computing
Network Development

Automated Reasoning
Embedded Systems
Data Engineering
Mobile Development
Game Development
While team placement is based on business needs, sharing your specific skills and interests helps us better align your experience with potential roles.

Collaborate and communicate effectively with experienced cross-disciplinary Amazonians to design, build, and operate innovative products and services that delight our customers, while participating in technical discussions to drive solutions forward.
Break down complex, ambiguous problems into well-defined, solvable components before implementation
Contribute to the design and development of scalable, reliable services, with distributed-systems scope varying by team.
Participate in code reviews as a core engineering practice, providing constructive feedback and validating correctness, including for AI-generated code.

Key Focus Areas
Developing AI-powered systems for automated product safety assessment and compliance verification
Building intelligent catalog management solutions using natural language processing and computer vision
Creating generative AI tools to enhance seller safety and compliance processes
Designing scalable architectures that combine traditional services with AI/ML capabilities
The Ideal Candidate Will Have
Strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with distributed systems
Knowledge of machine learning frameworks and generative AI technologies (e.g., transformers, LLMs)
Experience with AI model deployment, optimization, and monitoring in production environments
Ability to tackle complex problems through data-driven experimentation

Opportunity to work with state-of-the-art AI technologies and shape their application in e-commerce

Full-stack development experience across AI and traditional systems
Collaboration with international teams of applied scientists, engineers, and product managers
Innovation-focused environment with emphasis on continuous learning and experimentation

Conceive, design, build, test, and own software systems that automate investigation and compliance workflows at scale.
Design and code the right solutions starting from broadly defined problems, driving the technical direction of your work.
Build scalable, fault-tolerant, low-cost distributed systems for storage, indexing, prediction, and query.
Integrate AI/ML and GenAI capabilities into production, with attention to deployment, optimization, and monitoring.
Troubleshoot and support what you build, and work in an agile environment to deliver high-quality software.

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Preferred Qualifications
3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44534.description_preview:
Bitdeer is a world-leading technology company for AI and Bitcoin mining infrastructure.
Bitdeer is committed to providing comprehensive Bitcoin mining solutions for its customers and building AI computational infrastructure to support the AI revolution. Bitdeer handles complex processes involved in computing such as equipment procurement, transport logistics, data center design and construction, equipment management, and daily operations. Bitdeer also offers advanced cloud capabilities to customers with high demand for artificial intelligence.
Headquartered in Singapore, Bitdeer has deployed data centers across multiple countries, including the United States, Norway, Bhutan, and Ethiopia.
To learn more, visit https://ir.bitdeer.com/
Position Overview
Bitdeer is building an AI-operated GPU cloud — a global fleet of self-built and OEM-rented data centers running the world's most valuable compute, run by a platform that observes, protects, and operates the fleet. The SRE Platform team builds the monitoring and automation substrate that every other squad — storage, network, GPU, K8S, and L1 operators — depends on. Their signals become the system you help build.
As an entry-level Software Engineer on the SRE / Monitoring Platform team, you contribute to the NeoCloud SRE platform — the multi-region system that observes, protects, and operates a GPU rental fleet across self-built and OEM-rented data centers. You join a bounded context led by a senior engineer, take well-scoped components from design to production code that ships through GitOps + the CICD release pipeline, follows the Plugin Framework conventions, meets declared SLOs, and stays drift-free.
This is a build + learn role. You write code, write tests, and operate what you build under the guidance of a senior engineer. You participate in on-call as a shadow before taking primary. Within 12 months, you should be delivering components independently within your assigned area and growing toward owning a sub-context.
Key Responsibilities
Where you'll contribute (guided by a senior engineer)
Collection + Storage — help build collection-agent, metrics-store / logs-store / traces-store / profiles-store, enrichment-service, collection-monitor. Write ingestion, query, and storage-path code.
Alert + Correlation + SLO — contribute to alert-engine-framework, alert-correlation, slo-framework; implement and tune default alert rules.
Topology + Cluster-Health — contribute to topology-service, cluster-health-rollup, OSS-SRE-tool collection plugins for K8s / Slurm / Ray / Volcano / Kueue / KubeRay.
Remediation + Workflow + Jobs — help build remediation-actuator, orchestration / workflow components, inspection probes, job-scheduler.
Observability instrumentation — instrument services with metrics, logs, and traces via OpenTelemetry; build dashboards; write runbooks an on-call can follow.
Test discipline — write unit / integration / contract tests for everything you ship; participate in chaos and soak tests led by senior engineers.
Why this is a great first role
Greenfield with a well-defined vision. The Plugin Framework, GitOps pipeline, and SLO framework are decided; you build components inside them with a clear blueprint — not from a blank page.
You learn the full observability stack at production scale — ingest, query, storage — by building it, not just using it.
Mentorship-heavy. You work directly with senior and principal engineers who own the architecture; their expertise becomes your growth path.
Job Requirements
0-2 years of software engineering experience (new graduates with strong projects or internships welcome).
Solid fundamentals in one programming language — Go (preferred), Python, Java, or Rust. You can write clean, tested, readable code and explain your design choices.
CS fundamentals — data structures, algorithms, concurrency, basic networking (TCP / HTTP), and operating-system concepts (processes, threads, I/O). You can reason about correctness and performance.
Distributed systems basics — you understand the ideas behind idempotency, retries, back-pressure, caching, and eventual consistency, even if you haven't operated them at scale yet. Eagerness to go deep.
Monitoring / observability exposure — some hands-on with Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, or similar; can write a basic PromQL query and instrument a service. Eagerness to learn the ingest, query, and storage path of a real observability stack.
Familiarity with Linux and the shell; comfort reading system logs and using standard debugging tools.
Kubernetes basics — understand Pods, Services, Deployments; have run something on K8s (a project, lab, or internship).
Git + CI basics — branching, pull requests, and have used a CI pipeline (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or similar).
Test discipline — you write unit and integration tests as a habit, not an afterthought.
Communication — clear written and verbal English; can write a good PR description and ask good questions.
Curiosity and a learning mindset — the most important qualifier. You're excited to learn GPU / AI infrastructure, AIOps, distributed systems, and observability at production scale.
Nice-to-Haves
Internship or project in monitoring / observability, telemetry pipelines, or platform / SRE tooling.
Exposure to GPU / AI-infra — DCGM, InfiniBand / RoCE, Kubernetes GPU Operator, Slurm / Ray. Interest counts more than depth.
Exposure to AIOps / ML-adjacent tooling (anomaly detection, alert correlation).
Contributions to open-source observability or cloud-native projects.

An Agentic AI Engineer designs, builds, and deploys autonomous AI systems that can reason, plan, use tools, and execute multi-step workflows with minimal human intervention . Unlike traditional AI/ML engineers who focus on model training and prediction, agentic AI engineers orchestrate goal-driven workflows that integrate models, tools, memory, and business logic to achieve objectives dynamically
Core Responsibilities
Design & Develop Agentic Systems: Build intelligent agents capable of autonomous planning, reasoning, and task execution, often using LLMs (e.g., GPT-class, LLaMA), multi-modal models, and autonomous workflows
Orchestration & Frameworks: Implement agent orchestration using frameworks like LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, or custom solutions
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Design and optimize RAG pipelines for enhanced reasoning with external knowledge, including document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector stores, and retrieval ranking
Tool & Memory Integration: Develop agents that call APIs, databases, and other tools, maintain memory, and adapt based on outcomes
Evaluation & Monitoring: Create evaluation frameworks for accuracy, grounding, latency, and cost; build observability for agent behavior and failure modes
Model Adaptation: Fine-tune or adapt foundation models (e.g., via LoRA, adapters) for domain-specific use cases
Production Deployment: Deploy GenAI/agentic systems in cloud-native environments with CI/CD, versioning, and runtime safeguards
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with data scientists, ML engineers, product teams, and governance/compliance stakeholders
Required Skills & Experience
2+ years in AI/ML system design, deployment, or autonomous agent development
Programming: Proficiency in Python (and sometimes Java, C#) for AI/ML solution development
Agent & Workflow Expertise: Experience with agent orchestration frameworks and multi-agent communication protocols
RAG & LLM Integration: Hands-on with RAG architectures, evaluation methodologies, and LLM integration
Cloud & DevOps: Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., Azure, AWS) and CI/CD pipelines
Governance & Compliance: Understanding of responsible AI, security, and compliance in regulated domains (e.g., retail)

The Interplanetary Sciences Program was established to expand access to scientific exploration across our solar system. By creating a sustainable model for interplanetary exploration, we are transforming space science from an occasional event into a continuous process of discovery that accelerates knowledge, broadens participation, and inspires the next generation of explorers.
About The Role
The Interplanetary Sciences Program is building the operations software that will optimize the mission science and innovate in how we operate the spacecraft. The software will command, monitor, and coordinate the spacecraft, its science instruments, and its communications systems across the Mars 2028 mission. At Relativity Space, we set audacious goals. The Mars 2028 mission is designed to transform how we conduct interplanetary science missions bringing AI models to run on the spacecraft in Mars orbit. The instrument suite will sense the atmosphere to inform weather models and probe the surface with Radar to understand the location of ice. The mission operations for the Mars 2028 mission will also be ground-breaking with automation across the whole stack to enable autonomous science collection meaning the spacecraft can be re-tasked to acquire follow-up observations based on analysis and inference of recent data on the flight hardware.
As a Software Engineer – Operations, you will design and build the tools that mission operators, instrument teams, and external partners rely on every day from command generation and validation, to telemetry and data dissemination, to the interfaces that let outside teams safely and reliably interact with our systems. Description
Amazon Leo is closing the digital divide with a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites bringing fast, affordable broadband to communities the internet has never reliably reached. The customer terminal is the phased-array antenna at the customer's premises that turns that constellation into a working internet link — and our team writes the embedded software that makes it work: acquiring a LEO satellite on a fast overhead pass, electronically steering the beam to track it, closing and holding the link, and handing over to the next satellite within seconds. This is a broad role — you can work across the full signal chain and go deep wherever interests you most.
What You'll Work On
Electronic beam steering & tracking — real-time control that keeps a phased-array beam pointed at a fast-moving satellite across the pass and through every handover.
Phased-array calibration — per-element amplitude/phase calibration that holds beam and sidelobe performance across unit-to-unit variation, temperature, and frequency, on real hardware in the field, with the automated test coverage to keep it reliable.
Link acquisition, tracking & management — satellite acquisition, closed-loop tracking, and the control that brings the link up, keeps it healthy, and reacquires cleanly through handovers.
RF power & thermal management — managing transmit power and duty cycle against PA and platform thermal limits so the terminal runs at full performance without exceeding its envelope.
System integration & field telemetry — integrate the RF front-end, controls, and signal path, then use device telemetry to debug and improve terminals operating on orbit.
Key job responsibilities
What We Look For
Embedded C/C++ or Rust on Linux/RTOS, close to the hardware.
Wireless / RF / DSP exposure — phased arrays, beamforming, SatCom, 5G/LTE, radar, or similar — or strong drive to grow into it.
Hands-on hardware debugging — comfortable with lab instruments, RF test setups, and reading telemetry to reason about a live system.
Our Stack
Rust, C/C++, and Python on embedded Linux / RTOS, working directly with the RF front-end and real hardware — lab terminals, RF test benches, and satellites on orbit. Automated hardware-in-the-loop testing and rich fleet telemetry let you see the impact of your code in the real world. New development is increasingly in Rust.

As part of our BSP software engineering team, you will design and implement embedded software used in the Project Kuiper products. You will work in a collaborative environment with teams inside and outside of Amazon. You will craft your software from requirements, designs, code, test, to product deployment. You need to be flexible and responsive to changing priority issues.

The Kuiper Customer Terminal Software Team supports the devices that connect our customers to the Kuiper network. We provide software for both applications and the underlying Linux system. We work hand in hand with hardware, product and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers.

Experience with Embedded Coder and automatic code generation from Simulink models

Description
Do you want to help millions of customers protect their cloud workloads? The AWS security services team is building the next generation of security monitoring products that give customers a unified view of threats, risks, and compliance across multiple cloud environments. As a Software Development Engineer II on this team, you will design and build integrations that connect internal and external services, ingest infrastructure metadata and security findings at scale, and solve complex problems around data correctness and cross-provider modeling differences. With the rapid expansion of AI reshaping how customers manage security, there has never been a more compelling time to join — our team is investing heavily in delivering the right information, at the right time, with the right context so customers can understand risk and prioritize remediation faster.

Design and build service integrations using industry-standard authentication protocols such as OAuth and OpenID Connect (OIDC) to establish secure connectivity with internal and external platforms.
Develop data ingestion pipelines that collect infrastructure metadata, context, and security findings across multiple cloud providers, solving challenges around scale, data correctness, and cross-provider modeling differences.

Mentor peers and junior engineers through thoughtful code reviews and design feedback, championing software quality best practices across the team.
Own operational health for the services you build maintain alarms, dashboards, and runbooks, participate in on-call rotations, and ensure root causes of operational issues are permanently resolved.

You will operate with a high degree of independence on a roadmap-driven team. 3+ years of contributing to new and current systems architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) experience

onsemi

Validation Engineering is responsible for planning and executing product validation activities that confirm sensor performance, functionality, reliability readiness, and manufacturability from early silicon through production release. Develop and improve validation test methodologies, automation, and data analysis flows to detect issues early, reduce debug cycle time, and support robust product release decisions.
Enhance the performance and usability of existing validation tools by improving scripts, automation, documentation, and reporting workflows.
Support failure analysis, root-cause investigation, and cross-functional debug activities as key components of the validation engineering role.

This position is specifically looking for someone who is enrolled in a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or doctoral program in Electrical Engineering or related field with emphasis on chip level circuit design.
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering in progress, or related field with coursework on analog and digital circuit design.
Solid understanding of semiconductor device physics.
Proficient in scripting languages (e.g. Python, VB, Perl, C, bash).
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong team player and ability to work well in a collaborative environment.
Experience with Electrical lab equipment (e.g. oscilloscopes, power supplies, power meters, signal generators).
Familiarity with CMOS Circuit design and test methodology preferred.
Understanding of imager sensor architecture and product reliability requirements preferred.

Job Summary
As an AI Prototyping Engineer on the LATC team, you will be the creative and technical engine that turns emerging AI ideas into tangible, working demonstrations. You will operate at the intersection of research, product, and business — rapidly building proof-of-concepts, validating technical feasibility, and communicating findings to both engineering teams and business stakeholders. This is a hands-on role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, moves fast without breaking trust, and loves making complex AI capabilities feel real and accessible.
Responsibilities
Rapid Prototyping Experimentation
Design, build, and iterate on AI agent prototypes and interactive demos that showcase novel capabilities across Lenovo's product ecosystem (mobile, edge, enterprise).
Explore cutting-edge agentic frameworks, LLMs, and multimodal models to evaluate their fit for Lenovo's use cases.
Maintain a "prototype-first" mindset — ship working demos in days, not months.
Design, implement, and test components for a AI‑driven development ecosystem, including model‑powered tools and platform services that enhance the software delivery lifecycle.
Develop intelligent agents and automated workflows that streamline software build, testing, deployment, and operational tasks across CI/CD pipelines
Define, evaluate, and unify APIs, namespaces, and integration patterns across contributions from multiple developers, ensuring consistent interface design and long‑term architectural coherence within the platform.
Develop/integrate platforms for AI models and agent behaviors assessment for performance, accuracy, robustness, and fairness, and provide actionable insights to improve reliability and developer experience.
Technical Feasibility Research Translation
Conduct hands-on technical investigations of new AI models, tools, and frameworks, and produce clear feasibility reports summarizing findings, trade-offs, and recommendations.
Work closely with the LATC RD team to translate research outputs into prototype-ready implementations.
Identify promising technologies early and advocate for their adoption or de-risking.
Cross-Team Collaboration
Partner with Business Group (BG) product teams to understand real user needs and translate them into prototype specifications.
Act as a technical bridge between LATC technology pillars and business stakeholders, ensuring prototypes address genuine product priorities.
Work closely with mentors and team members to document findings, share insights, and contribute to non-coding project deliverables.
Stakeholder Communication
Present prototype demos and technical findings to internal stakeholders, including department leaders and BG partners, in a clear and compelling way.
Create supporting materials (slide decks, short videos, written summaries) that communicate the "so what" of each prototype.
Gather feedback from demos and rapidly incorporate it into the next iteration.
Engineering Craft
Write clean, well-documented prototype code that can be handed off to production engineers when a concept is validated.
Contribute to shared tooling, reusable components, and internal knowledge bases that accelerate future prototyping cycles.
Required Qualifications
3–5 years of software engineering experience, with at least 1 year focused on ML/AI systems or LLM-based applications.
BS/MS in Computer Science, AI/ML, or related field; equivalent practical experience considered.
Strong Python skills, including experience with async patterns and working with AI/ML libraries.
Hands-on experience with agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or AutoGen.
Demonstrated ability to build functional AI prototypes or demos quickly, ideally with examples to show.
Comfortable working in ambiguous, fast-moving environments with shifting priorities.
Strong communication skills — able to explain technical concepts to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.
Experience working across teams and gathering requirements from product or business partners.
A portfolio of demos, side projects, blog posts, or open-source contributions showcasing AI work.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with multimodal models (vision, speech, or on-device AI).
Background in edge or mobile AI deployment (latency-constrained environments).
Familiarity with MCP (Model Context Protocol) or similar agent communication protocols.
Experience with MLOps tools or experiment tracking frameworks (MLflow, WB, etc.).
Comfort with presentation tools and an eye for communicating ideas visually.

The Accelerator Operations and Technology Division (AOT), Radio Frequency Engineering (RFE) group is seeking an R&D Engineer 2 or 3 for the Low-Level Radio-Frequency (LLRF) team.
The AOT division maintains, operates, and upgrades all accelerator systems used at the Los Alamos Neutron Science Center (LANSCE) complex. These consist of two 750-keV Cockcroft-Walton-based injector systems (H+ and H- systems), a 201.25-MHz drift-tube linear accelerator (LINAC) utilizing high-power diacrode tubes, an 805-MHz coupled cavity LINAC utilizing high-power klystrons as the primary power source, a proton storage ring, and roughly a kilometer of beam transport lines that deliver beam to the five independent research programs. The RFE group is principally responsible for all radio frequency (RF) systems and their associated amplitude and phase control in relation to the accelerating beam.
Due to the different types of equipment that we are involved with, when working in AOT-RFE no day is the same as the next. Members of the LLRF team are involved in the design, construction, testing and installation of high-frequency electronics and software systems dedicated to the control of RF waveforms to achieve optimal acceleration and bunching of the beam. The LLRF team works on ultra stable frequency sources, solid-state and vacuum tube based amplifiers, temperature controlled coaxial lines spanning the length of the accelerator, electronics detecting the beam amplitude at the injector, resonance control systems compensating for cavity changes due to RF heating and fast electronics meant to prevent a cavity arc from damaging amplifiers producing megawatts of power.

We hire for attitude over experience!
About Lulius Innovation
Lulius Innovation builds software products for Army Aviation and other parts of the military: readiness, training, and records tools that operators, maintainers, and commanders depend on. Our products run under DoD security requirements, deploy from schoolhouses to operational units, and are growing fast, with new capabilities in active development. We're a small, veteran-owned team, and we're hiring a junior software developer to build alongside us.
If you learned or started to program alongside AI, that is not a mark against you. It's how we work. What we do require is that you understand, and own, every line the agent helps you write. You should be able to read a component and know why it re-renders, follow a request through a function API to the database and back, and spot when generated code is wrong, insecure, or quietly solving the wrong problem.
What you'll do
Build features across the full stack: React and Next.js interfaces, Node.js and Express services, and PostgreSQL data models.
Write the code yourself, using AI coding tools to assist with planning, testing, and refactoring, and review every change before it goes up for code review.
Write and maintain tests, fix bugs, and track problems down across the browser, the API, and the database.
Build, run, and debug our products locally in Docker and Docker Compose, the same way they run in the field.
Work in Git with the team's branching, commit, and pull-request practices, and take part in code reviews in both directions.
Write code that holds up under a DoD security posture: input validation, access control, audit trails, and no secrets in the repo.
Learn the military mission well enough to build what operators, maintainers, and commanders actually need.
The stack
Our products are containerized JavaScript from front to back, PostgreSQL, Tailwind and shadcn/ui, Zustand for state, and Highcharts for visualization, all running in Docker on Linux. You don't need all of it on day one. You need enough of the fundamentals that the rest is learnable, and the curiosity to go learn it.
What you bring
Working knowledge of JavaScript​: promises and async/await, modules, closures, and how the event loop shapes a Node.js server.
Hands-on React: components, props and state, hooks, and how rendering works. Next.js experience is a strong plus.
Node.js fundamentals: building REST APIs, handling requests and errors, and managing configuration across environments.
Basic SQL and relational data: you can write a join, read a schema, and reason about a migration before you run it.
Experience using AI coding assistants to support your own work, and the judgment to verify their output instead of trusting it.
Comfort with Git, the command line, Linux, and containers, or a clear willingness to get comfortable fast.
Something you built, with or without AI, that you can walk us through line by line: a GitHub repo, a deployed app, a class project, or work from an internship or bootcamp.
Eligibility for a Government background check and CAC issuance for access to DoD systems.
Military experience would be phenomenal, but it is not required. If you've served, especially in Army Aviation, you already understand the people we build for: how a unit runs, why readiness data has to be right, and what it costs when software gets in the way. That perspective makes you a better developer here from day one. If you haven't served, that's fine too. We'll teach you the mission, and a fresh set of eyes has its own value. Veterans, transitioning service members, Guard and Reserve members are strongly encouraged to apply.
DoD SkillBridge
Lulius is a DoD SkillBridge partner. If you're a service member in your final 180 days of service, you can apply to spend that time training and working with us through SkillBridge (the Career Skills Program for Soldiers), keeping your military pay and benefits while you build real experience on our products. With positions just outside Fort Rucker and in Reno/Tahoe, plus a remote option, many transitioning service members can do it close to where they already are. Talk to your command and transition office about eligibility, then reach out to us to set it up.
How we'll get to know you
In interviews, expect to walk us through something you built: how it works, where AI assisted, and what you had to fix when it got things wrong. We may ask you to extend it live with your own tools. We're looking for understanding and judgment, not memorized syntax.
Location and details
This is a full-time position based in Reno/Tahoe, Nevada, or in Daleville, Alabama, just outside Fort Rucker and close to the Army Aviation schoolhouses and units we build for. Remote is also an option for the right U.S.-based candidate. You'll work with our engineering team in Reno and Huntsville, with occasional travel to Fort Rucker, Redstone Arsenal, and supported units. Lulius Innovation is a veteran-owned small business headquartered in Reno/Tahoe, Nevada, building for Army Aviation and the broader military.
How to apply (bot check: please read)

LinkedIn Easy Apply submissions without a matching application on our site will not be considered. About Dexmate
Dexmate is building the foundation for physical AI — combining a new generation of robots with a universal Physical AI OS, making robots as easy to build and deploy as software. Today, robotics is fragmented, slow, and closed: most builders are forced to reinvent the same stack again and again, and most ideas never make it past the prototype stage. We exist to change that. If you want to help shape the next layer of human capability — and believe the future of robotics should be built together, not in isolation — we'd love to build it with you.
THE ROLE
We're looking for an Embedded Systems Engineer to own the boundary where our robot's electronics meet its software. You will bring up and debug new PCBs, write the firmware and drivers that make every sensor, camera, actuator, and compute module talk to each other, and make sure data moves reliably across CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, GMSL, I2C, SPI, and Ethernet.
This is a hands-on, cross-layer role. One day you're probing a board with a scope to find why a bus is dropping frames; the next you're writing a Linux driver for a camera serializer or tuning an EtherCAT network for deterministic timing. You'll work closely with electrical, firmware, controls, and robotics software engineers, and you'll often be the person who figures out whether a problem lives in hardware, firmware, or software.
Responsibilities
Bringing up, validating, and debugging new PCBs: reading schematics and layouts, measuring signals, and isolating hardware vs. software faults
Developing firmware for MCUs (bare-metal and RTOS) and drivers for embedded Linux platforms (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson / Orin)
Writing and maintaining device drivers and communication stacks for CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, I2C, SPI, UART, and Ethernet
Integrating camera and sensor pipelines over GMSL (serializer/deserializer configuration, device trees, V4L2 drivers, timing and synchronization)
Bringing up and tuning EtherCAT and CAN networks across actuators, sensors, and power systems for deterministic, real-time performance
Debugging signal-integrity, power, timing, and bus-level issues with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and protocol analyzers
Contributing firmware and software input during schematic and PCB design reviews to make boards easier to bring up, test, and debug
Building diagnostics, test fixtures, and automated hardware-in-the-loop tests for boards and subsystems
Supporting manufacturing, end-of-line testing, and field troubleshooting as robots move from prototype to deployment
Documenting interfaces, bring-up procedures, and debugging playbooks for the wider team
Minimum Qualifications
3+ years of professional experience in embedded systems in robotics, automotive, industrial automation, or complex consumer electronics
Strong C and C++ skills for firmware and driver development; working knowledge of Python for tooling and test automation
Hands-on board bring-up experience, including reading schematics, PCB layouts, datasheets, and timing diagrams
Driver-level experience with several of: CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, I2C, SPI, UART, Ethernet
Experience with MCU firmware (ARM Cortex-M, STM32, TI C2000, or similar) on bare-metal or RTOS platforms
Comfort with embedded debugging and lab tools: JTAG/SWD debuggers, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and protocol analyzers
Systematic debugging skills across the hardware, firmware, and software boundary
Strong communication skills and comfort working directly with electrical, mechanical, controls, and software engineers
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with GMSL or other high-speed camera links (e.g., MAX9295/MAX9296, FPD-Link), MIPI CSI-2, and V4L2
Embedded Linux kernel and device-driver development, device trees, and BSP bring-up (NVIDIA Jetson / Orin a plus)
Experience integrating EtherCAT master or slave stacks (SOEM, IgH, or equivalent)
Familiarity with PCB design tools (Altium, KiCad) and the ability to propose schematic-level fixes
Knowledge of signal integrity, power integrity, and EMC fundamentals
Experience with motor-control, BMS, or power-electronics systems
Experience with ROS 2 or other robotics middleware
Prior experience working in a vertically integrated robotics or hardware startup
Hands-on use of AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex to accelerate implementation, debugging, testing, and documentation

America is critically deficient in production of defensive munitions- we currently produce shipborne interceptors in the few hundreds per year while our adversaries are producing offensive threats in the tens of thousands per year. Furientis was started to help solve this problem- introducing a new class of cost-effective, high production rate, interceptor missiles. We're seeking motivated individuals who internalize this problem and are eager to apply their past experience in similar industries (aerospace, defense, automotive/racing, robotics) and out of the box thinking to solve this problem for the US and its allies.
About The Team
The Seeker Team builds the eyes and the targeting logic of our weapon system: a low-cost, mass-producible, multimodal missile seeker that leans on commercial supply chains where they outperform, and vertically integrates wherever possible. On a modern missile, the seeker is 40 to 60% of unit cost and often drives overly long delivery cycles; accordingly, the seeker team is at the tip of the spear for delivering capability to our customers and value to the taxpayer.
Seeker design has exactly two real constraints: physics and mission. Nothing else is a show-stopper, only an obstacle to overcome. We are a small, deeply technical team that drives capability through ingenuity and bias for action and ships hardware that flies. This is a wear-many-hats environment where you must be comfortable "building the airplane in flight" and stepping well outside your comfort zone; a narrowly scoped role with clean handoffs is not what this team offers.
This is an AI-native team. Through fluent use of cutting-edge agentic coding tools, one engineer here consistently out-delivers a much larger conventional team. You will have opinions about where these tools help and where they do not, provide governance input, and build out an AI-centric workflow from day one.
About The Role
You will contribute to the production of perception and estimation algorithms at the core of our seeker: detection, tracking, classification, and aimpoint localization on infrared (IR) imagery and fused sensor measurements, against targets that fight back. As part of the Seeker Team, you will research, implement, optimize, and validate algorithms in these areas, including modern AI and machine learning (ML) methods where they earn their place. Runtime efficiency is a hard constraint: everything you build must run within a strict latency budget on embedded flight-compute hardware. You will work closely with the broader Seeker Team to carry your algorithms from first prototype into flight.
What You'll Do
Design and implement object detection algorithms for mid-wave infrared (MWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) imagery, robust to clutter, domain shift, and countermeasures.
Develop multi-object tracking and state estimation: filtering, data association, and line-of-sight estimates for missile guidance.
Implement track lifecycle management: initialization, maintenance, confirmation, and termination under real sensor conditions.
Develop segmentation, classification, and discrimination algorithms that separate targets from decoys, debris, and background.
Develop aimpoint localization and the associated image-processing methods that support terminal accuracy.
Contribute to perception-related sensor fusion, combining IR and X-band radar measurements into a consistent track picture.
Implement, optimize, and validate your algorithms for real-time flight: measured latency, covariance and confidence you can defend, and performance proven in simulation, in hardware-in-the-loop testing, and in flight data.
Research and prototype advanced AI and ML methods within perception and estimation, and help mature the ones that prove out into the flight pipeline.
Skills We're Hiring For
Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Applied Math, Physics, or a related field; Master of Science (M.S.) or Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) preferred.
5 to 7 years of experience in applied computer vision, perception, or estimation on real sensor data.
Fluency in state estimation: the Kalman filter family, including nonlinear variants and interacting multiple model (IMM) approaches, applied with judgment.
Data association at multi-target scale: joint probabilistic data association (JPDA), multiple hypothesis tracking, or modern equivalents, chosen with judgment.
Classical optical image and signal processing as a working toolkit, with emphasis on methods for optical sensors: spatial and temporal filtering, morphology, non-uniformity and fixed-pattern noise handling, and techniques for imagery with a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
Statistical rigor as a habit: normalized estimation error squared (NEES) and normalized innovation squared (NIS) consistency testing, covariance validation, and calibrated confidence.
3+ years of experience using python to create, alter, and maintain libraries of algorithms within a modern Git & CI/CD framework.
Bonus Points For
Rust for real-time implementation and familiarity with embedded CUDA
Missile, interceptor, or guided-munition perception or tracking experience.
Track-before-detect or other methods for detection and tracking at low SNR.
IR or other non-visible-band sensor experience, including synthetic-to-real domain adaptation.
TensorRT or comparable edge inference deployment experience.
Multi-sensor registration, boresight exploitation, or radar measurement familiarity.
Modern machine learning fluency (PyTorch or equivalent): training, evaluating, and shrinking perception models with measured accuracy tradeoffs.
Daily use of agentic coding tools (Claude Code or similar) to multiply your output.
Eligibility & Logistics
Location: On-site at our Los Angeles, CA HQ; remote work is not available. Monthly weekend travel for test events and supplier engagements. Clearance: A clearance is not required for this position. Must be a U.S. Person

Senior Software Engineer - Cards

As the story goes, in 1949 Frank McNamara finished dinner at a New York restaurant and found he'd left his wallet in another suit. His fix was a card that let members eat now and pay later. That card became Diners Club, widely credited as the first multipurpose charge card. It was a piece of cardboard and a promise: the restaurant trusted the card, the card trusted the member, and someone had to make sure the money actually moved.
More than seventy-five years later, the promise hasn't changed, but the machinery has. When a Mercury customer taps their card, the request goes from the merchant's terminal through an acquirer and a card network to us. In a fraction of a second, we check the balance, apply the customer's spend controls, screen for fraud and say yes or no. After that comes clearing, settlement, disputes and reporting, and every cent has to reconcile.
Cards
are
the way Mercury customers spend money. The Cards Integration team owns the whole Mercury card, not just the swipe: issuance, physical card shipping, spend controls, lifecycle management, authorization, money movement, settlement and reporting, and the infrastructure underneath. We're a full-stack team, and our job is to make the Mercury Debit and IO cards reliable, correct, useful, and innovative.
We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who thinks deeply about systems architecture, cares about the customer experience, and will dive into any problem to move the team forward. We value high ownership, working in pairs and teams rather than alone, and attention to detail. Lead projects from idea to tech spec to implementation to launch, working with your PM, EM, tech lead, and teammates at each stage. When you lead a project, it's yours to see through.
Learn how debit and credit cards actually work under the hood (authorization, clearing, settlement, disputes) and use that knowledge every day.
Build features across the stack, from the card experiences customers use to the backend systems that move money.
Help keep our operations excellent. Our systems are some of the most observable at Mercury, and with great observability comes great responsibility.
Mentor other engineers and raise engineering quality through design reviews, code reviews, and collaboration.
Work with product, design, operations, risk, compliance, sales, and many other teams.
You should
Have strong full-stack experience, a product mindset, systems thinking, and a knack for getting things across the line.
Have made architectural decisions on complex systems, and be able to explain your reasoning and the trade-offs.

Description
Training and running large AI models takes enormous amounts of expensive accelerated compute, and most of it sits idle. Across the industry, a large share of GPU capacity is paid for but never does useful work because jobs cannot find it, cannot share it, or cannot see it and use it efficiently. We build the services that closes that gap.
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build the systems that put idle or inefficiently used GPUs to work. You will design and build distributed backend services that let organizations pool capacity across many clusters and accounts, route it to the workloads that need it most, and see exactly how it is being used. This is deep systems work at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, container orchestration, and cloud infrastructure, and it directly changes how much value customers get from every GPU they pay for.
You will own services end to end, from design through launch and operation in production, and your work will ship to some of the largest AI compute customers in the world.
Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and operate distributed backend services that manage and share accelerated compute across multiple clusters and accounts.
Build scheduling and capacity-sharing capabilities that move compute to the highest-priority workloads and reclaim it when priorities change.
Build zero-touch usage and guidance systems that collect, aggregate, and report how compute is consumed, at scale and in near real time.
Own your services in production: define operational metrics, respond to issues, and continuously improve reliability, latency, and cost.
Write clear design documents, participate in design and code reviews, and raise the engineering bar for the team.
Collaborate with product, design, and partner engineering teams to turn customer problems into shipped features.
Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of ownership, quality, and customer focus.
A day in the life
Most days start with a short team stand-up, then it is mostly building. You might design a service that lets one cluster borrow idle capacity from another, then write it up for a design review where the team pokes holes in it before any code is written. Hard problems get their own deep-dive whiteboard session. Other days lean toward operations, chasing down why a workload did not get the capacity it should have. You will not be handed fully specified tasks; you will have the independence to help decide what to build, then build it.
About The Team
We help customers get the most out of the accelerated compute they pay for. Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make sure every accelerator a customer pays for is doing useful work, and make that easy to see and control. Cost reduction is one important part of that, but the bigger idea is the engine that delivers compute to the workloads that need it most, in as little time as possible.
Our customers run some of the largest AI training and inference workloads in the world, and they feel the impact of our work directly in how much they can do with their infrastructure. We care about depth, we own our work end to end, and we build in the open where we can.

Overview
Susquehanna is looking for a Virtualization Engineer to help design and build infrastructure for our trading platforms on OpenStack. You will work closely with other infrastructure engineers and software developers to create scalable systems.
What You'll Do
Automate and Evolve:
Contribute to our library of home-grown tools, written primarily in Python and Bash, utilizing tools such as Jenkins to automate bare-metal and virtual server deployments, monitoring, and maintenance, allowing you to focus on performance related issues and projects.
Optimize:
Tune virtualization environments for performance and network stacks for throughput and latency. Dive deep on root-cause analysis of systems issues. Anything is fair game if there's impact.
Collaborate:
Work closely with stakeholders to understand business problems. Implement scalable solutions using SAN and high-speed networks.
Create:
Design and implement our next-generation VM platform in OpenStack which is slated to replace our 18000 guest VMWare environment.
Monitor:
Effectively track and display cluster capacity to ensure optimal performance. Forecast and prepare for increased resource demands. Develop tools that best fit our needs for monitoring and capacity planning.
What We're Looking For
A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related discipline.
1-5 years of progressive experience building Linux based platforms at scale.
Familiarity with kernel-level and I/O subsystem tweaks and tools such as sysctl, strace, tcpdump, and netstat.
Recent hands-on experience with automation in Python, required
In-depth experience in open-source-based virtualization such as OpenStack, RedHat Openshift, kubevirt, or similar.
About Susquehanna
Susquehanna is a global quantitative trading firm founded by a group of friends who share a passion for game theory and probabilistic thinking. We have incorporated this approach into our culture, where you will find relentless problem solvers within each of our core disciplines: Trading, Technology, and Quantitative Research. From offices around the world, our employees collaborate to make optimal decisions and are driven by the desire to achieve winning results together.
What We Do
We are experts in trading essentially all listed financial products and asset classes, with a focus on derivatives trading. Through market making and market taking, we handle millions of trading transactions around the world every day, providing liquidity and ensuring competitive prices for buyers and sellers. While our presence in the market is broad, our trading desks are highly specialized, allowing for a deep understanding of unique drivers of each asset class.
Susquehanna does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or search firms. Any resume or referral submitted in the absence of a signed agreement will become the property of Susquehanna and no fee will be paid.

Role Mission
Mid-training sits at the seam between pre-training and post-training and is one of the highest-leverage points in the entire model pipeline. This is where raw base model capability is sharpened into something that can reason deeply, generalize reliably, and serve as the foundation that post-training builds on.
You will own the late-stage training decisions that determine what our models are fundamentally capable of: data mix and quality uplift, annealing schedules, context length extension, capability injection across coding, math, and reasoning, and the synthetic data strategies that make all of it scale. This role does cross-cutting work across what is classically considered both pre-training and post-training. We don't distinguish between research and engineering; we expect both.
What You'll Accomplish
Data Mix and Quality Uplift: Design and iterate on high-quality data mixtures for late-stage and annealing training runs. Develop principled methods for sourcing, filtering, and weighting data to sharpen model capabilities without degrading general performance.
Capability Injection: Drive targeted improvements in coding, mathematics, and long-horizon reasoning through curated data strategies and training interventions. Translate research insights into measurable capability gains on our agents.
Synthetic Data Research: Develop and evaluate synthetic data pipelines that generate training signal at scale. Understand the limits and failure modes of synthetic approaches and build methods that hold up in production training runs.
Annealing and Schedule Design: Research and optimize multi-stage learning rate schedules, warmup strategies, and compute allocation across training phases. Understand how schedule choices interact with data distribution and model behavior.
Context Length Extension: Research and implement methods for extending effective context length without degrading short-context performance. This includes positional encoding strategies, data construction, and targeted evaluation.
Evaluation and Iteration: Build evals that distinguish real capability improvements from benchmark overfitting. Close the loop between training decisions and what actually matters for Devin and our other systems in deployment.
Scaling and Methodology: Measure how mid-training interventions scale with compute and data. Develop new approaches when existing methods hit ceilings; we expect both rigorous empiricism and original thinking.

Experience developing or evaluating synthetic data pipelines for capability improvement

Strong fundamentals in optimization, statistics, and ML theory; able to distinguish real effects from noise, instability, and overfitting
A track record of original contributions: publications, open-source impact, or internal results that moved a capability frontier
Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where the problem definition is as important as the solution
We care more about demonstrated capability than credentials. A PhD is one signal among many.

About The Team
The GPT Infrastructure team builds systems that turn advances in model inference and optimization into reliable production capabilities. We enable OpenAI workloads to be qualified and optimized across new accelerator platforms without requiring a one-off port and tuning effort for every hardware target.
Our work spans distributed systems, model execution, compilers and runtimes, performance engineering, secure partner integrations, evaluation systems, and developer tooling. We build the infrastructure that makes optimization workflows automated, reproducible, and trustworthy.
About The Role
We are seeking a software engineer to help build the platform that qualifies and optimizes inference workloads across heterogeneous compute environments.
You will develop both OpenAI-hosted services and secure partner-side software for running long-lived optimization workflows. These workflows generate candidate kernels, runtime configurations, and serving-stack changes; compile and execute them on target hardware; verify their correctness; measure their performance; and use the results to guide further optimization.
You will work across model architecture, distributed execution, compilers, runtimes, networking, and accelerator systems. Financial institutions process billions of transactions every day across cards, ACH, wires, and third party aggregators. But most of that data is difficult to use. Descriptions are inconsistent, merchant names don’t match, and categories vary by payment type.
Spade is a data and AI platform that turns messy transaction strings into structured, verified records — and gives teams the tools to act on it across authorization, attribution, analytics, and AI initiatives. Spade leads the market in terms of merchant coverage, matching accuracy, geolocation data, and speed of transaction enrichment. The Opportunity
As a Full Stack Engineer at Spade, you’ll own product experiences end-to-end, working across both the frontend and backend of our enrichment platform. You’ll build customer-facing interfaces in React and TypeScript, as well as the Python/Django APIs, data models, and platform services that power them. About AIUC
AIUC builds standards and insurance for frontier AI. Our mission is to Underwrite superintelligence. We exist because risk, not capability, is becoming the binding constraint on AI being useful. History offers lessons for how to build confidence in new technology; electricity burned down houses until insurers funded Underwriters Laboratories (UL) to certify products against their standards. Today, the UL mark is a trustmark on every light bulb in America. We’re building that for AI.
AIUC-1, our standard for agent security, serves frontier builders like Cursor, Lovable, ElevenLabs, and Harvey. We've raised $55m from Ribbit, First Harmonic and Nat Friedman to audit frontier AI. Our team comes from METR, Anthropic, McKinsey, and OpenAI. Come join us.
The Role
Every AI company that comes to us wants the same thing: proof their agent is safe enough to sell to an enterprise. Getting there means running thousands of evaluations against their live system.
We've now certified the category leaders in every major AI vertical: ElevenLabs (voice), Intercom (customer service), UiPath (workflow automation), Lovable (coding), and more we'll announce soon. No two of those systems look alike: each has its own authentication, its own interface, its own definition of what a failure even looks like. Before we can test any of it, someone has to sit with that customer, understand how their agent actually works, and get it wired into our evaluation system.
We're hiring an
engineer to own that work end to end
. You'll have your own set of customers within your first weeks, paired with a commercial counterpart on each one.
In This Role, You Will
Own the path from signed customer to delivered results - scoping what to test, working through their authentication and interfaces, and getting their agent running in our system
Build the one-off version when a customer doesn't fit the product yet, and make it work anyway
Deliver results directly to the customer and be the person they trust with the technical detail
Make the call on whether a customer meets the AIUC-1 standard
Work across the widest surface of any role here: our Delivery team, our core engineers, sales, the Standards team (shaping what goes into AIUC-1), and your customer's own engineering team
Turn what you learn in the field into the product
That last one is why the role exists. We're building toward a product that runs evaluations end to end without an engineer in the loop. This is a high-agency role: you'll shape what we build next as much as you'll deliver what we've built.
If you're planning to start a company one day, this is a front row seat. You'll work directly with our founders, with founders at the companies we certify, and alongside a team full of ex-founders.
What We're Looking For
The job in practice looks like reading someone's API docs, chasing credentials, building integrations into customers' systems and agents. Then evaluating whether those agents behave, and owning the failure modes the evals surface. The person who thrives here has done this work before. What drives them is trust and safety.
To Be Successful, We Think You Have
3-7 years of experience, likely as an early engineer at a startup where you ended up owning customers, or in an integration, solutions, or forward deployed role selling technical products to technical buyers. (Impact matters more than years.)
Enough software engineering to build and debug an integration yourself, and the judgment to know when the scrappy version is the right answer
Comfort owning a customer relationship directly – scoping the work, setting expectations, and delivering bad news early
Customer obsession: their problem is your problem, and you see it through
The discipline to turn what you see in the field into something reusable rather than solving the same problem twice
Nice to have
Experience founding or co-founding a company
Experience with AI evaluations or red-teaming
Executive presence with senior stakeholders
Our Values
We are in the business of building trust. We take our values seriously and treat them as commitments to each other, held to the same bar as the ones we make to customers.
Strong back: high standards, keep our promises, work hard.
Fast feet: experiment, cut scope, take delight in pace.
Eyes up: wrestle with the mission, and let where AI is heading shape our strategy, our teams and our day-to-day work.
Open heart: say the scary thing, create connection, make room for emotions.
Underwriting superintelligence is our life's work. If you want it to be yours, apply now.
Compensation & Perks
Competitive annual salary
Equity (significant part of total compensation)
Health, dental and vision insurance for you and your dependents
Visa sponsorship and relocation stipend to bring you to SF, if needed
Daily lunch, dinner & snacks

Which sensor measurements feed the model.
How that information is stored and retrieved in SQL or Oracle.
What physical relationships and assumptions drive the calculations.
How calculated targets reach Level 1 controls and influence equipment operation.

Review process trends and compare model predictions with actual operating results.
Apply thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, calculus, and differential equations to investigate process behavior.
Develop and troubleshoot C# code supporting process models and operating setups.
Use SQL or Oracle to retrieve sensor histories, investigate abnormalities, and validate model inputs.
Determine whether a performance issue comes from sensor data, model assumptions, software, or changing process conditions.
Work with metallurgists, operators, Level 1 controls engineers, and equipment suppliers to refine process targets.
Test and document model changes, then evaluate their effect on quality, consistency, and throughput.
Support commissioning and continued tuning as equipment and production conditions evolve.

Strong understanding of applied physics, calculus, differential equations, and numerical methods.
Experience translating engineering calculations or mathematical models into software.

Ability to explain why a model works, recognize its limitations, and validate it against measured results.
Interest in working onsite with the equipment and people affected by your software.
